title: Privacy and customer confidentiality
audience: Any worker or employer who handles customer and staff personal information in any service business.
learningOutcomes: Identify the personal information that a service business collects and holds.
Describe the confidentiality practices that protect that information in daily work.
Explain what to do if personal information is lost, sent to the wrong person or accessed without authority.

instruction.heading: What counts as personal information
instruction.body: Personal information is information about an identifiable person. In a service business it includes names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, schedules, access codes, photographs of people or homes, household details, payment details and staff records. Think of anything that would let someone identify or locate a person, or learn about their home, as personal information. Keep it only for the purpose of delivering the service, and only for as long as the business needs it.

instruction.heading: Confidentiality in daily work
instruction.body: Keep customer and staff information out of conversations, messages and social media that are not part of the job. Do not leave documents or screens visible in a customer's home, and do not discuss one customer's information with another. Use only the approved systems. Lock devices when you leave them. Send information only to the person who needs it, and check the address before you send it. Do not keep copies of personal information on a personal device or account.

instruction.heading: Breaches and the privacy position
instruction.body: A privacy breach occurs when personal information is lost, sent to the wrong person, or accessed without authority. If it happens, stop the activity that caused it where possible, recover the information if you can, and report it to the designated contact immediately. The business decides on any notification to the customer or the regulator. The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner states that the Privacy Act applies to organisations above the $3 million AUD annual turnover threshold, and that small businesses at or below that threshold are generally outside it.

procedure: Identify the personal information you collect and hold for the job, and keep only what is needed.
Keep the information in the approved system and do not copy it to personal devices or accounts.
Check the recipient before sending any information, and send only what that person needs.
Keep documents and screens out of view of other people in the home or site.
If information is lost, sent to the wrong person or accessed without authority, report it to the designated contact immediately.
Record the breach facts and the actions taken, and follow the business's breach procedure.

workedExamples.situation: You send a schedule email to the wrong customer, which includes another customer's address and access code.
workedExamples.reasoning: Report it to the designated contact immediately, ask the wrong recipient to delete the email, and record the facts, including what was sent and when. The business decides on any notification to the affected customer and whether the change of access code is needed.

commonErrors.error: Sending personal information to the wrong address.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the recipient before sending, and send only what is needed.

commonErrors.error: Keeping customer photographs on a personal phone.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the approved system only and delete copies according to the procedure.

commonErrors.error: Not reporting a breach because it seems minor.
commonErrors.prevention: Report every breach to the designated contact immediately.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner states that the Privacy Act applies to organisations above $3 million AUD annual turnover and that small businesses at or below that threshold are generally outside the Act.
Some sectors, such as healthcare, aged care and child-care, may have specific confidentiality rules.

qualityStandard: Personal information is kept only in the approved system and only for the job.
Each transmission of personal information is checked for the right recipient.
Every breach is reported to the designated contact immediately and recorded.
documentationEvidence: Breach record with the facts, the information involved, the actions taken and the people notified.
Record of any access or deletion request handled through the approved channel.
summary: Personal information includes names, addresses, codes, photographs and household details.
Keep it confidential, in the approved system, and sent only to the right person.
Report any breach immediately; the business decides on notifications.

knowledgeChecks.question: You send a customer's details to the wrong person. What should you do first?
options: Report it to the designated contact immediately and record the facts.
Wait to see whether the recipient reports it first and then decide.
Forward the message to a colleague to see what was sent today

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should customer photographs be stored?
options: On a personal phone for convenience.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say about discussing one customer's information with another customer?
options: Discuss it to speed up the job
It is allowed if the two customers are friends
It is allowed when a neighbour asks
Do not discuss one customer's information with another

officialReferences.title: Small business (Office of the Australian Information Commissioner)
officialReferences.covers: Read via summary fetch in this pass. Defines a small business as one with annual turnover of $3 million or less, and says a small business at or below that threshold is generally not covered by the Privacy Act on turnover alone. Other criteria can bring a business in, such as trading in personal information without consent or being a health service provider. The page uses the $ symbol and does not name the currency. It recommends protecting personal information as best practice. Proposed threshold changes: UNCONFIRMED (not addressed on the page read). Publisher: OAIC.
